inputs: The three Appendix B vectors of the 2000 Camellia specification with 128-, 192- and 256-bit keys and the common plaintext 0123456789abcdeffedcba9876543210
expected: Every encryption matches the listed ciphertext and every decryption returns 0123456789abcdeffedcba9876543210; the 128-bit key uses 18 rounds with 4 kw, 18 k and 4 ke subkeys, and the 192/256-bit keys use 24 rounds with 4 kw, 24 k and 6 ke subkeys
limitations: Three fixed vectors; they cover all three key lengths but only one plaintext, and a match does not prove resistance to cryptanalysis.

inputs: The KL/KR definitions for the three key lengths, the 192-bit complement construction, and the KA/KB, kw, k and ke values computed for the 128-bit test key
expected: 128-bit KL=0123456789abcdeffedcba9876543210 and KR=0; 192-bit KR=0011223344556677ffeeddccbbaa9988; 256-bit KR=00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff; 128-bit KA=ae71c3d55ba6bf1d169240a795f89256 and KB=6408e232ac24708fcc3a213a704bd393; sample kw1..kw4, k1..k4, k17, k18 and ke1..ke4 as recorded in vectors.json; the decryption schedule reverses kw, k and ke
limitations: One published key length (128 bits) is checked against recorded computed samples; the 192/256-bit values are checked by their vectors and structural properties, not by published intermediate subkeys.

inputs: Tables 4-7 of the 2000 specification, the derived s2/s3/s4 definitions, and deterministic samples for S, P, F, FL and FL^-1
expected: All four tables have 256 entries; s2(x)=s1(x)<<<1, s3(x)=s1(x)<<<7 and s4(x)=s1(x<<<1) reproduce all 256 entries of Tables 5-7; s1[0x3d]=86; S(0123456789abcdef)=821f66b4b6f9daa4, P(0123456789abcdef)=aaeeaaeeabcdef89 and F(0123456789abcdef,0)=d7e110581ab139a3; FL(0123456789abcdef,fedcba9876543210)=fedcba9889abcdef and FL^-1 returns the input for all 256 deterministic samples
limitations: Structural and reproducibility checks, not an assessment of S-box nonlinearity or cryptographic strength.

inputs: Three key lengths times eight deterministic plaintext patterns, including the official plaintext, with fixed test keys
expected: All 24 encrypt/decrypt round trips return the plaintext; the same plaintext under different keys gives different ciphertexts; the 128-, 192- and 256-bit keys produce distinct schedules; and the 192- and 256-bit test keys, which share the left 128 bits, produce different KA and KB values
limitations: Deterministic round-trip tests only; they do not test modes, protocols, key management, side channels or randomness.
